hooks.text: A piece of the Moon's blinding face is sitting in Madagascar.
The bright rock covering the Moon spans forty square miles in Madagascar.
Why is the Moon's brightest crust sitting exposed in southern Madagascar?

title: The Moon Rock Hiding in Madagascar
description: The bright highlands of the Moon are made of anorthosite, an ancient rock that also forms a massive white formation in Madagascar. Astronauts photographed the forty-square-mile geological wonder from the Space Station.

beats.text: Over four billion years ago, light minerals floated on a magma ocean to form the Moon's crust.
beats.visual: Artist concept of the magma ocean covering the early Moon, 2019

beats.text: Apollo astronauts hauled back tiny fragments, forcing researchers to hunt for larger rock analogues on Earth.
beats.visual: Apollo 15 astronaut collecting lunar anorthosite samples on the Moon, 1971

beats.text: While smaller deposits sit in Montana, southern Madagascar holds an exposure of unprecedented scale.
beats.visual: Anorthosite rock outcrop in the Stillwater Complex of Montana, 2018

beats.text: Astronauts aboard the Space Station photographed a brilliant, forty-square-mile white circle blazing against the landscape.
beats.visual: Astronaut photograph ISS075-E-85249 showing the white Saririaky massif from orbit, 2026

beats.text: Formed 600 million years ago, this massive dome survived ancient continental collisions.
